episode_title: Episode 107: State of the Firm, Version 2026
question: Why did Lois LLC transition from fully remote to hybrid work with three days in-office requirement in 2026?
transcript_excerpt: Greg made the transition because he determined that full remote work was not healthy for employees, leadership, or professional development. He stated: 'I said at the end of last year, I said, no, this is not working for us long term. It's not healthy for the employees. It's not healthy for the leadership of the company. And it's just not great for developing mastery.' The hybrid model with three days per week in-office, flexible within their New York or New Jersey offices, aims to build stronger values-based organization and enable better mentoring and capacity building.

episode_title: Episode 107: State of the Firm, Version 2026
question: What practice area did Lois LLC close in 2026 and why?
transcript_excerpt: Lois LLC closed its profitable New Jersey workers' compensation practice area in 2026 to focus exclusively on New York. Greg explained: 'We said, look, we want to put all of our wood behind one arrow, and that arrow is being amazing in New York and not kind of amazing in New York, but we also have these other practices that we have to tend to grow and develop.' The firm stopped accepting new New Jersey referrals and is running down the existing profitable practice to consolidate resources and build best-of-breed expertise in a single jurisdiction.

episode_title: Episode 107: State of the Firm, Version 2026
question: What AI infrastructure has Lois LLC built internally rather than using cloud-based systems?
transcript_excerpt: Lois LLC has built an on-premises artificial intelligence system connected to over 1.1 billion documents in their document management server and their SQL-based practice management software. Greg stated: 'we own all the documents, over 1.1 billion documents in our document management server. We have our own data that runs our SQL-based practice management software, and now we've connected that to an on-premises AI brain.' The firm runs its own data centers, off-premises disaster recovery, dedicated fiber lines between offices, and has been running its own private cloud for eight years without using external vendors, ensuring no client data goes into public cloud systems like ChatGPT or Gemini.

episode_title: Episode 107: State of the Firm, Version 2026
question: What are the five main business process areas Lois LLC has converted to machine-ready logic for AI deployment?
transcript_excerpt: Lois LLC has reduced five main focus areas into machine-ready business logic: (1) determining average weekly wage and rate calculation for each case, (2) scheduled loss of use calculations, (3) loss of wage earning calculations, (4) Medicare compliance screening, and (5) the entire risk transfer process automation. Greg explained: 'we have five main focuses that we have reduced all the business logic into machine logic' to prepare for training internal AI systems, ensuring the firm can deploy intelligence at scale in a safe, controlled way using only internal data.

episode_title: Episode 107: State of the Firm, Version 2026
question: What security risks did Greg identify with cloud-based AI systems like ChatGPT in legal practice?
transcript_excerpt: Greg identified that ChatGPT and similar systems use user prompts and responses to train their models, creating a security vulnerability where attorneys' innovative legal strategies and case work product can be weaponized against their own clients. He cited ChatGPT's recent admission about solving a 200-year-old mathematical problem: 'it turns out that mathematicians were actually using ChatGPT to try to figure out how to answer this math problem. Well, it turns out that mathematicians were actually using ChatGPT... and ChatGPT now admits, well, we did. Actually, we might have leveraged some of the questioning and the logic patterns that were put in by our users.' He also expressed skepticism about vendor claims of zero data retention policies and HIPAA compliance, stating these create unnecessary risks around medical information transmission.

episode_title: Episode 107: State of the Firm, Version 2026
question: How does Lois LLC plan to use AI for case strategy through red teaming in 2027?
transcript_excerpt: Lois LLC plans to use its on-premises AI as an adversarial tool to red team cases by instructing the AI to argue from the opposing counsel's perspective. Greg explained: 'we would just say, hey, look at our system and here's the case we want to talk about and say, now you, AI, you're going to be my adversary. You're going to be the plaintiff's attorney and let's red team the case.' This allows less experienced attorneys to understand adversary arguments at scale and anticipate opposing strategies, replacing the time-intensive mentorship-based approach previously used for training.
